transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-24
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (EchoHealth - Head of ML), James Lee (EchoHealth - Platform), Olivia Chen (EchoHealth - Security), Noah Rivera (EchoHealth - PM)

Summary (auto-gen): Discussed cost modeling approach for the POC, agreed on representative prompt set and benchmark metrics, and outlined a 2-week pilot schedule.

00:00:00 - Samira: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a quick intro then jump into the cost model and POC scope
00:00:18 - Maya: Hi all, thanks, we've got a hard constraint on monthly infra budget and a target latency for our clinician UI, so keen to understand tradeoffs
00:00:30 - Diego: Great, I'll focus on the technical knobs (batching, KV cache, quantization) and how those map to per-token and p95 latency numbers, Samira will cover commercial and next steps
00:00:52 - James: Quick note, our typical request distribution is 70% short prompts (~50 tokens), 25% medium (~256 tokens), 5% long (~1024 tokens)
00:01:12 - Noah: Our SLA target is p95 <= 300ms for the 256 token case, and we want to keep the per active-user cost under $3 / month for inference costs alone
00:01:35 - Diego: Okay that distribution is super helpful, we'll size the POC bench off that. One thing up front: hosted vs dedicated vs private changes unit economics alot — hosted gives fastest time-to-value, dedicated reduces per-token costs with reserved capacity, and private adds security but increases ops cost, and maybe slightly higher latency depending on on-prem network
00:02:05 - Olivia: For security, SOC2 is required and we need to see audit logs and KMS integration. If we go private we have to ensure HSM/KMS integration with our key management
00:02:25 - Samira: Noted — we'll share our SOC2 summary and the security pack, and the dedicated/private runbooks. Back to cost: Diego, can you walk through the per-token estimates we typically see?
00:02:40 - Diego: Sure. High-level buckets: model inference compute, batching efficiency, KV/prefix cache savings, and overlay infra. For a hosted setup on a 13B-type open model baseline, you might see O( $0.0004 - $0.001 ) per generated token depending on seq len and concurrency. With dedicated reserved capacity and quantization we often get that down to ~ $0.00008 - $0.00025 per token. These are rough ranges — the POC benchmark will give concrete numbers for EchoHealth's prompt mix
00:03:28 - Maya: That range is wide, can you show how batching and caching change it for our mix?
00:03:40 - Diego: Absolutely. Example: for short prompts batching pushes throughput up but adds queuing latency; with a concurrent arrival rate that matches your 70/25/5 mix, moderate batching (batch size 8-16) plus prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts can reduce generation tokens by ~25-40% effective cost. For the 256-token median case, enabling KV cache for repeated context could drop compute tokens by 30% which yields linear savings on per-token cost.
00:04:22 - James: We're curious about tail latency impact. If we batch aggressively to get costs down, do we blow the p95?
00:04:34 - Diego: There's a tradeoff. For low-latency UI needs we recommend dynamic batching with SLO-driven time windows: small batches for p95-sensitive routes (e.g., clinician realtime) and larger batches for asynchronous tasks. Redwood's runtime supports per-route policies so you can have both. In the POC we'll test two profiles: low-latency profile (batch timeout 8ms, max batch 4) and cost-optimized profile (batch timeout 40ms, max batch 16) and measure p95 and tokens/second
00:05:10 - Maya: Good. Can you explain the KV cache a bit more? We have a lot of repeated system prompts and patient templates
00:05:20 - Diego: KV cache stores the key/value cache for transformer layers for prefix tokens across requests. If many requests share the same system prompts or repeated scaffolding, we avoid re-computing the prefix which reduces compute proportionally to the prefix length. For your system where the first 120 tokens are often identical, that's a big win
00:05:45 - Olivia: Any data residency implications for prefix cache? If we cache keys in a shared pool do we leak PHI across tenants?
00:05:55 - Diego: We can partition caches by tenant; with private or dedicated you get tenant isolation. For hosted we offer per-customer caches with encryption-at-rest. We'll detail this in the security pack.
00:06:14 - Samira: On the financial side, EchoHealth asked for an example unit economics sheet — we'll send a model that takes observed token counts, hit rates for KV, batch efficiency, and maps to monthly $/active user. The POC will validate the parameters
00:06:34 - Noah: For POC size, what's realistic? We can allocate a staging fleet, but we want the results to be predictive of production at 10k DAUs eventually
00:06:46 - Diego: For throughput scaling, we usually run benchmark runs that emulate your production concurrency: e.g., 1k concurrent sessions with arrival distribution matching your mix, and measure throughput and p95. For the POC we'll run bench at smaller scale (representative) then extrapolate. We'll also run a production-like run with burst traffic to validate autoscaling and fallback policies
00:07:20 - Maya: Bench methodology — please be explicit. We need reproducible scripts and the prompt set.
00:07:28 - Diego: We'll provide the runbook: the 3-stage bench: 1) warmup to populate caches, 2) steady-state run (15 mins) to measure p95/throughput, 3) spike test. We'll use your 1k sample prompts (you'll share repository) and synthetic ramp scripts. We'll publish raw logs and aggregated metrics
00:07:50 - James: About quantization — does Redwood support int8 or int4 quant profiles? We care about latency and quality tradeoffs
00:07:58 - Diego: Yes, we have multiple quant profiles. For the POC we'll try 8-bit quant and 4-bit quant candidate for the 13B model. 4-bit reduces memory and can improve throughput but sometimes has small quality deltas; we'll run A/B on the prompt set to measure regession rates
00:08:20 - Maya: What's the expected perf delta between hosted and dedicated in your experience?
00:08:30 - Samira: Hosted is great for getting started; dedicated reduces variability and per-token cost because you control reserved GPU pools and can pack instances. Historically customers see 1.5-3x cost improvements going dedicated when utilization is high and you can tolerate a commit. We'll show a worked example in the cost sheet
00:08:55 - Olivia: Network — if we go private, we need VPC peering and strict egress rules. We also require audit logs to be forwarded to our SIEM
00:09:05 - Diego: Understood. Redwood Private supports VPC peering and audit log streaming to S3 or your SIEM. We'll include the network checklist in the security doc packet
00:09:20 - Noah: Timeline — what's the POC cadence?
00:09:28 - Samira: We propose a 2-week POC: Week 1: env setup, collect prompt corpus, baseline runs; Week 2: benchmark runs, iterate on batching/quant & KV config, then a final analysis and readout. We can compress if EchoHealth wants an accelerated schedule
00:09:48 - Maya: That works. Who owns the staging infra?
00:09:54 - Diego: Redwood can provision a dedicated test cluster in our cloud for the bench. If you prefer private network, we can do a VPN/VPC peering to your cloud. For initial bench hosted/dedicated is fastest
00:10:10 - James: Any rough dollar numbers for the POC itself? We need to put in a budget request
00:10:18 - Samira: The POC cost to you is typically the usage of the test cluster plus an implementation services estimate. For a 2-week POC with benchmark runs and SE time it's often in the range of $6k-$12k depending on fleet size and SE hours; we'll spell that out in the follow-up email
00:10:37 - Maya: Good. On success criteria: concrete items we'd like to include — p95 < 300ms for 256 tokens, <1% hallucination rate on the eval set, monthly inference cost projection < $X per active user (we'll supply the target), and no blocking security findings
00:10:58 - Diego: We'll measure p95, throughput, tokens per second, model quality using your eval prompts and an automated scoring rubric, and produce a regression report.
00:11:14 - (small cross-talk)
00:11:30 - Diego: Quick example numbers for your mix: assume average response tokens generated is 220 per medium request. With KV cache hit rate 40% for the 120-token prefix and batching efficiency at 1.6x (effective tokens per GPU second improvement), an 8-bit quantized model on dedicated pool could yield ~$0.00012 per generated token. Without quant and on hosted you might be at ~$0.00055/token. Important caveat: these numbers are illustrative — we'll validate in bench
00:12:18 - Maya: How do we extrapolate from bench to production 10k DAU? Is the model linear?
00:12:27 - Diego: Mostly linear with GPU throughput, but caching gives nonlinear wins because more repeated prefixes at higher scale increases hit rates for shared prompt types. Also autoscaling dynamics and tail latencies need a margin — we'll include safety factors in the model and run a predictive scenario analysis in the cost sheet
00:12:50 - Noah: On instrumentation — we need token-level cost and latency breakdown in console for billing and alerts
00:12:59 - Samira: Redwood Console exposes per-route token costs, latency percentiles, trace links and can export data to your analytics. We'll demo console in the POC readout
00:13:12 - Olivia: For compliance, will you sign a DPA and process PHI under BAAs?
00:13:20 - Samira: We have BAA discussions in enterprise sales and specific private deployments can be structured to meet PHI needs. We'll get legal looped in once we finalize scope
00:13:35 - James: Any pitfalls customers hit during POC?
00:13:40 - Diego: Common ones: not providing representative prompts (leads to optimistic caching gains), not warming caches before steady-state runs, and mixing asynchronous and real-time routes in the same profile. We call these out in the runbook
00:13:58 - Maya: Let's talk deliverables — what will you hand us at the end?
00:14:06 - Samira: Deliverables: 1) raw benchmark logs + aggregated metrics, 2) cost model populated with measured parameters and production projections, 3) quality/regression report on your eval set, 4) runbook and recommended config for your production rollout
00:14:24 - Noah: Perfect. Any decisions on which models to try?
00:14:30 - Diego: We'll test two open-weight candidates: a 13B quantized and a 7B as a faster low-cost variant. We'll run A/B to check quality. We'll include a fallback policy to a cheaper model for non-critical work
00:14:45 - Maya: For prompts with PHI, can we redact before sending to hosted endpoints?
00:14:52 - Olivia: We prefer token-level redaction and forwarding only non-PHI context when possible
00:15:00 - Diego: Redwood supports customer-side pre-processing; we can include a redaction step in the runbook. For private/dedicated you can keep raw data in your VPC and not leave network
00:15:15 - Samira: Ok wrapping up — let me recap the agreed items and timeline. We will: send cost model sheet (Samira), Redwood to provision test cluster and runbench (Diego), EchoHealth to share prompts and security constraints (Maya/Olivia), target benchmark run 2025-06-30 and follow-up on 2025-07-02 with results
00:15:41 - Maya: Sounds good
00:15:45 - James: A couple more quick questions about pricing model commitments — if we go dedicated what's the minimum commit?
00:15:52 - Samira: Typical reserved capacity starts at a monthly commit equivalent to a few GPUs; exact numbers depend on throughput targets. We'll include a worked example in the cost sheet comparing pay-as-you-go hosted vs 6/12 month reserved pricing
00:16:10 - (brief side conversation about calendar invites)
00:17:00 - Diego: I'll also add two bench profiles to the repo: low-latency and cost-optimized, and we'll run both to show tradeoffs.
00:17:18 - Maya: Appreciate it. Anything else?
00:17:22 - Olivia: Please include the security contact and the specific SIEM integrations you support
00:17:30 - Samira: We'll include Rachel in Security ops; attaching security pack with endpoints for SIEM, KMS and audit log streaming
00:17:40 - Noah: OK great.
00:17:46 - Samira: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the sheet and schedule.
00:17:52 - (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions of product names (e.g., Redwood Dedicate vs Redwood Dedicated) and speaker overlaps; see security pack referenced at https://redwood.ai/security-pack and cost sheet template at https://redwood.ai/pocs/cost-model-template (placeholders).
